detailed_description:

The target video is exactly 15 seconds long in 16:9. Use grounded live-action cinematic youth-film photography, natural teenage features, realistic skin texture, restrained acting, shallow depth of field, subtle film grain, and a warm amber-and-muted-blue palette.

All shots occur continuously during the same late-afternoon minute. Lock white balance at 5000K and use fixed manual exposure, fixed contrast, and one consistent film curve.

The sunlight always enters from the large windows on screen-left and produces soft warm rims with neutral skylight fill on both faces. Maintain stable facial brightness, window highlights, uniform colors, and shadow density across every cut.

Use precise Mandarin lip synchronization and allow each speaker to close their mouth naturally after completing a line.

[Shot 1] From 00:00.000 to 00:03.000, begin with a medium-close side view of <Subject 1> (S1) standing beside a desk near the left windows inside <Subject 3>.

Her navy backpack is already worn correctly on both shoulders. One open notebook and one pen rest on the desk.

She places the pen horizontally into the notebook's inner fold with her right hand while her left palm holds the page flat. She closes the notebook once with both hands and lifts it securely against her lower chest.

Her gaze remains on her hands. Her expression is calm and slightly tired after class.

At 00:02.000, the classroom door opens softly behind her. Her hands stop only after the notebook is secured. Her eyes move toward the sound first, followed by a small turn of her head over her right shoulder.

Her eyebrows lift subtly as she recognizes someone at the door. Cut only after her gaze reaches the doorway.

[Shot 2] From 00:03.000 to 00:06.000, cut along her eyeline to an over-the-shoulder composition from behind <Subject 2> (S2) at the doorway, looking toward <Subject 1> (S1) beside the sunlit desk.

The boy's shoulder and backpack strap remain softly focused in the right foreground while the girl is sharp.

<Subject 1> (S1) turns her shoulders slightly toward him without leaving the desk. Her initial surprise softens into curious familiarity.

After one brief breath, she asks in a natural, lightly surprised tone, <d>[Chinese] 你怎么还没走？</d>

Her lips close naturally after the question. She maintains eye contact, tilts her head by only a few degrees, and waits rather than immediately moving.

[Shot 3] From 00:06.000 to 00:09.000, cut to a chest-up reverse close-up of <Subject 2> (S2) standing just inside the classroom doorway.

His navy backpack remains worn correctly on both shoulders. His left hand holds the left backpack strap. His right hand has released the door handle and lowers naturally to his side.

He meets her gaze, hesitates for half a beat, and gives a small closed-mouth smile. His brows soften and his shoulders release slightly.

In a gentle, matter-of-fact voice, he says, <d>[Chinese] 等你啊。一起走？</d>

His delivery is quiet and sincere, not teasing or theatrical. He closes his mouth naturally after the question.

He then shifts backward by one small step and rotates his torso toward the corridor, creating a clear path beside him while continuing to look at her.

[Shot 4] From 00:09.000 to 00:12.000, cut back to an intimate three-quarter close-up of <Subject 1> (S1).

She absorbs his answer without speaking immediately. Her eyes widen by a very small amount, then lower toward the closed notebook in shy acknowledgment.

She presses her lips together briefly, takes one quiet breath, and looks back toward him. Her cheeks lift and a sincere restrained smile appears.

She answers softly, <d>[Chinese] 嗯，走吧。</d>

Her lips close into the same small smile. Only after finishing the line does she tighten both forearms around the notebook, turn her shoulders and hips together toward the central aisle, and take one complete first step away from the desk.

Her ponytail and backpack follow the turn with natural delayed motion. Cut on the beginning of her second step.

[Shot 5] From 00:12.000 to 00:15.000, match cut to a low waist-height two-shot looking diagonally down the central aisle toward the doorway.

<Subject 1> (S1) completes the same second step from [Shot 4], carrying the closed notebook securely against her torso.

<Subject 2> (S2) remains beside the open doorway, preserving the clear path he created in [Shot 3].

She approaches and passes through the threshold first. As their shoulders become level, her eyes turn toward him before her head follows slightly.

He returns her smile, lowers his gaze for a brief shy beat, then turns toward the corridor. He falls into step half a pace beside and behind her.

Their shoulders remain separated, their backpacks do not collide, and they do not touch.

The camera tracks forward slowly for less than one meter, holding their profiles and the warm classroom behind them.

End at 00:15.000 as both students continue naturally into the corridor at the same relaxed pace, with no additional dialogue or gesture.

Preserve <Subject 1> and <Subject 2>'s exact apparent high-school age, facial identities, hairstyles, uniforms, footwear, backpacks, voice characteristics, and body proportions.

Maintain one continuous classroom geography: windows on screen-left, doorway on screen-right, central aisle between desks, and sunset light traveling from left to right.

Keep the same notebook and pen, consistent backpack straps, physically correct hand contact, continuous walking direction, matched eyelines, matched foot movement, and clear speaking order.

overall_soundscape:

The dialogue is clean, close, and natural while retaining the acoustics of a real classroom.

Begin with distant cicadas, leaves outside the windows, a slow ceiling fan, faint corridor activity, page movement, the pen touching paper, and the dry closure of the notebook.

Synchronize the classroom door with one soft hinge movement and a restrained latch sound. Reduce the room tone slightly but do not mute it during each dialogue line.

In [Shot 2], include <Subject 1>'s small preparatory breath before speaking and a quiet room decay after her question.

In [Shot 3], include <Subject 2>'s half-beat hesitation, slight backpack-strap tension, and one soft backward step after his reply.

In [Shot 4], emphasize her quiet breath, subtle uniform fabric, notebook pressure, shoe pivot, and first step.

Carry the second step continuously into [Shot 5], then add two restrained sets of corridor footsteps, soft backpack movement, and slightly clearer corridor ambience as they leave.

Keep background voices unintelligible and spatially distant. No school bell, transition whooshes, or exaggerated footsteps.

non_diegetic_music:

An understated 15-second youth-film score at approximately 84 BPM, led by soft felt piano, lightly picked acoustic-guitar harmonics, a warm sustained string pad, and very restrained brushed percussion.

Begin with two sparse piano notes while <Subject 1> closes her notebook. Introduce a quiet guitar phrase when the door opens.

Reduce the music beneath all dialogue. Let a soft piano note follow her question and a warm guitar answer follow his reply.

Add a gentle rhythmic pulse only after she says <d>[Chinese] 嗯，走吧。</d>

Resolve into one warm suspended chord as they leave through the doorway. Keep the music youthful, intimate, hopeful, and below the dialogue and natural classroom ambience without becoming sentimental or melodramatic.
